A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COBRA and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Their methods, experiments and supplementary material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and few-shot experiments using TCGA training data and CPTAC evaluation cohorts, together with ablations and interpretability results.

after.justification: V3 retains and revises these original experiments, including classification results, few-shot evaluations, additional baseline comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The Mamba-2 architecture, attention pooling, contrastive objective and available inference procedures are retained. V3 selects the existing single-FM mode as its default and names the previously demonstrated unseen-FM procedure hybrid-FM; neither introduces a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: The TCGA/CPTAC cohorts, tissue domains and 15 clinical targets are retained. LUAD TP53 and KRAS already appeared in v1's appendix. The additional few-shot evaluations concern previously evaluated targets under smaller training samples, rather than new datasets or clinical tasks.

E2.justification: V3 adds Concatenated mean embeddings and Ensemble Prediction, which averages predictions from the four pretraining FMs, in Tables 2 and 6–9. These extend the comparisons with simple multi-FM alternatives while retaining the existing named slide encoders and mean-embedding baselines.

E3.justification: The default comparison switches from combined-FM to single-FM Virchow2 inference, and Table 2 averages all 15 targets rather than 13. Few-shot evaluation extends from six to ten existing targets, adding LUAD STK11, EGFR and TP53 and COAD sidedness. The k=5,10,25 budgets and TCGA-to-CPTAC evaluation design remain.

E4.justification: The encoded-versus-original embedding ablation changes its reported control from COBRA†-ENC, marked as using all four FMs, to COBRA-ENC explicitly based on Virchow2 (Tables 6–9). The other inference and magnification ablations, unseen-GigaPath evaluation, UMAP analysis and heatmap cases are retained.

E5.justification: Five-fold evaluation, ten random few-shot runs and numerical subscripts remain. However, v3 removes Table 2's explicit explanation that entries are fold means and subscripts are standard deviations, without supplying a replacement definition. No increase in runs or new statistical testing is documented.

E6.justification: Full-classification results are extensively revised across Tables 2–11. For example, Table 6 reports COBRA-V2 TP53 AUC as 40.4 in v1 and 78.4 in v3, contrasting with v1's statement of no predictive signal. Tables 12–23 add four few-shot targets and revise existing results, including GigaPath scores. The headline averages of 71.6 and 75.3 use different inference defaults and target sets, so they are not directly comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: The architecture, attention, InfoNCE and momentum-update mathematics are retained. Notation corrections and rearranged expressions for existing inference modes do not add mathematical reasoning, assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract updates the claimed average advantage over existing slide encoders from at least 3.8 to 4.4 AUC points on the revised comparison. The central contributions—unsupervised single-modality learning, data efficiency, compatibility with unseen FMs and flexible magnification—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds explicit limitations concerning restricted tissue and evaluation coverage, reliance on the contrastive objective, and linear aggregation of patch embeddings. It also qualifies combined-FM inference as offering marginal benefits at 0.5 MPP and greater benefits at lower magnifications, refining v1's interpretation.

D1.justification: V3 adds code-access information, specifies 50% downstream-classifier dropout, defines positive classes for AUPRC and F1, and expands inference instructions in Appendix B. These are additional disclosures; the documented pretraining hyperparameters, hardware and training duration remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds the Dosovitskiy et al. Vision Transformer reference. It also revises MADELEINE's described pretraining from 69,000 slides and breast/kidney coverage to 21,000 slides and breast-only coverage (Table 1 and Section 4.4). The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section organization are retained, with local wording and terminology edits. A new inference appendix shifts the existing appendix sections, and limitations, acknowledgments, competing interests and funding disclosures are added. This is a limited expansion rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to distinguish default and optional inference paths. Figure 2 retains its three cohort groups but changes its plotted aggregates and vertical-axis range. Tables gain comparator rows or task columns and are reflowed; the heatmap images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added multi-FM controls make the central comparison more informative, while inference guidance, positive-class definitions, code-access information and explicit limitations improve transparency. These provide a modest net benefit. Reporting defects limit the gain: v3 gives conflicting 5× COBRA†-V2 EGFR AUCs—82.9 in Table 3 versus 75.5 in Tables 4 and 10, where v1 agreed—and removes the uncertainty-subscript definition.
